troy terry.det: Terry (hip) has been placed to LTIR.
troy terry.long: With Terry's return not scheduled until mid-November at the earliest, the Anaheim Ducks have placed the 29-year-old winger on LTIR to start the season with a hip injury. Terry is entering his 10th NHL season and has not appeared in fewer than 60 games in any of the last five seasons. He enjoyed an impressive, yet shortened campaign in 2025-26, with 19 goals and 57 points across 61 games played.

ian moore.det: Moore (lower body) will miss the next 2-4 weeks.
ian moore.long: Moore was expected to be a key piece of the Anaheim Ducks' defensive unit after they lost a few big names in the offseason, but will have to wait for his regular-season debut after it was announced that the 24-year-old is expected to miss the next 2-4 weeks with a lower-body injury. The second-year defenseman is coming off an up-and-down rookie campaign, where he had four goals, 12 points, 24 PIMs and a -14 plus/minus across 67 games played. His spot is now up for grabs on opening night when Anaheim takes on the Vegas Golden Knights on October 2nd.

drew helleson.det: Helleson (lower-body) has been placed on IR.
drew helleson.long: Helleson will miss at least the next two games after Anaheim announced the 25-year-old had been placed on IR with a lower-body injury on Wednesday. The third-year pro is entering an important season, with the Ducks having never appeared in more than 60 games in any of his first two campaigns. When eligible to return, he will look to build off the two goals and 15 points he put up across 60 games last season.

charlie mcavoy.det: McAvoy is suspended for the first six regular-season games of 2026-27.
charlie mcavoy.long: McAvoy was suspended after the Bruins were eliminated from the playoffs last season for slashing Zach Benson in Game 6. McAvoy's absence means room for a young defenseman to crack the opening night roster like Frederic Brunet, who worked on PP2 on Tuesday. McAvoy will be eligible to return to the lineup in San Jose on October 13th.

conor timmins.det: Timmins (lower body) has been placed on IR.
conor timmins.long: Timmins has struggled to stay healthy at the NHL level, failing to surpass 52 games played in all but one of his seven seasons and will start the 2026-27 campaign on Injured Reserve with a lower-body injury. The 28-year-old appeared in 39 games for the Sabres last season, picking up eight assists, 18 PIMs and a -8 plus/minus.

alex lyon.det: Lyon (upper-body) left Thursday's preseason game vs. Detroit and did not return.
alex lyon.long: Lyon had a scare on Thursday, leaving Buffalo's preseason game vs. Detroit with an upper-body injury in the 2nd period. The 33-year-old is expected to be evaluated on Friday, as the Sabres update us on his status heading into their season opener vs. Columbus on October 1st. Lyon was expected to split time with Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen this season, but will likely be replaced by Colten Ellis if he is forced to miss any time.

jonathan huberdeau.det: Huberdeau (hip) is not expected to be ready for the start of Calgary’s training camp.
jonathan huberdeau.long: Huberdeau has been out since February 4th of last season due to a hip injury and is not expected to be ready for the start of Calgary’s training camp. The 33-year-old has struggled since arriving in Calgary four years ago, averaging just 15.5 goals and 48.5 points after finishing above 90+ points twice while previously in Florida. Calgary is still hopeful to have Huberdeau healthy and ready for the regular season, but the 14-year pro is already behind the eight ball with the latest news.

seth jarvis.long: Up to this point, Jarvis had been skating in a non-contact jersey, but he was a full participant in Thursday's am skate. Jarvis is not expected to play on Thursday, but this is a sign that his season debut could come in the not too distant future.

alexander nikishin.long: Nikishin is an unsigned RFA who has requested a trade from Carolina, so he will hold out of training camp while he awaits a new deal or a trade. The Hurricanes' bolstered their defensive depth recently by signing both P-O Joseph and Mike Reilly to one-year deals.

connor bedard.det: Bedard (shoulder) is participating in Chicago's practice on Monday in a non-contact jersey.
connor bedard.long: Bedard underwent shoulder surgery in early July and was given a four-month recovery timeline, but could be trending toward a sooner-than-expected return after practicing on Monday. The 21-year-old Bedard, the first-overall pick in the 2023 NHL Entry Draft, missed some time last season with a shoulder injury, but was exceptional when healthy, scoring 75 points (30G / 45A) in 69 games.

andrew mangiapane.long: Mangiapane suffered a lower-body injury in Chicago's season-opening game and has not played since. The 30-year-old forward was traded to Chicago last season after struggling with the Edmonton Oilers. He ended the 2025-26 season with 16 points (8G / 8A) in 62 games combined between the Blackhawks and Oilers.

logan o connor.det: O'Connor (lower-body) will be a game-time decision in Calgary on Thursday.
logan o connor.long: O'Connor has missed Colorado's first three games of the season with a lower-body injury but could make his debut on Thursday against the Calgary Flames. The 30-year-old is entering his eighth season in Colorado after only managing to appear in 13 games last season due to a hip injury. He will be a key part of the Avalanche's bottom-six when he is fully able to return to the lineup.

isac lundestrom.long: Lundestrom had Achilles surgery in July and remains out month to month, likely through the end of the calendar year. The 26-year-old Swedish forward averaged 12:23 last season in 68 games with the Blue Jackets, scoring 12 points (4G / 8A).

ivan provorov.det: Provorov (lower-body) is out for Columbus' season opener vs. Buffalo and is considered week-to-week.
ivan provorov.long: Provorov has been extremely durable over the past several seasons, playing all 82 games in four consecutive years, but he will start the 2026-27 season on the sidelines with a lower-body ailment. The 29-year-old defenseman averaged 24:49 time on ice, recording 31 points (9G / 22A) and 134 blocks last season in 82 outings.

dante fabbro.det: Fabbro (hand) is expected to miss at least one month.
dante fabbro.long: Fabbro sustained a hand fracture in the preseason and is expected to miss at least one month, opening the season on the Injured Non-Roster List. With Fabbro out, the Blue Jackets may sign Carson Soucy, who was with the team on a PTO during the preseason. Expect Fabbro to miss at least the first 10 games of the season.

The 35-year-old veteran battled injury concerns last season, playing just 57 games while scoring 45 points (16G / 29A). The Stars will again rely heavily on Duchene's offensive contributions in 2026-27.

j t compher.long: Compher did not play the previous game for the Red Wings due to an undisclosed injury, and has been retroactively placed on Injured Reserve. The 31-year-old Compher has spent most of his career as a bottom-six forward, but has been thrust into a more offensive role for the Red Wings. He scored 28 points (11G / 17A) in 82 games last season.

marco kasper.det: Kasper is week-to-week with an upper-body injury.
marco kasper.long: Kasper suffered an injury in the Red Wings' season opener. The 22-year-old Austrian forward has not played since and is expected to be sidelined week-to-week with an upper-body injury. After scoring 34 points (19G / 18A) in his rookie season in 2024-25, Kasper is coming off a disappointing 2025-26 campaign, scoring just 19 points (9G / 10A) in 81 outings.

mason appleton.det: Appleton is week-to-week with an undisclosed injury.
mason appleton.long: Appleton is battling an undisclosed injury and will be out week-to-week. The Red Wings are already lacking depth at center ice and can ill-afford to be without Appleton. The 30-year-old scored 14 points (6G / 8A) in 65 games with the Red Wings last season.

mattias janmark.long: Janmark missed the entirety of Edmonton's preseason action with an undisclosed injury and will remain out indefinitely after the team announced there was no timetable to return for the 33-year-old's return. Janmark is entering his 11th NHL season and was expected to play a complementary role in Edmonton's bottom-six after putting up a goal, eight points and 22 PIMs in 43 games last season.

matthew savoie.det: Savoie (undisclosed) has been placed on LTIR.
matthew savoie.long: Savoie did not participate in training camp due to an undisclosed injury, and is roughly eight weeks away from returning according to Head Coach Mike Babcock. The 22-year-old is coming off a strong rookie season in 2025-26 where he had 18-goals, 37 points and 25 PIMs in 82 games played.

ryan nugent hopkins.det: Nugent-Hopkins (lower-body) has been placed on IR.
ryan nugent hopkins.long: Nugent-Hopkins went down in practice on Monday with a lower-body injury. The 33-year-old is entering his 16th NHL season and is expected to approximately miss the first two weeks of the regular season. He was replaced by Vasily Podkolzin on Edmonton's top power-play unit in their opening game of the season.

zach hyman.det: Hyman (upper-body) returned to Oilers’ practice on Friday.
zach hyman.long: Hyman played 20:33 time on ice in Edmonton's season-opening 6-5 loss to the Vancouver Canucks on Tuesday, but has not played since due to an upper-body injury. He appears to be on cue to return for original two-week recovery timeline. The 34-year-old forward had a resurgent 2025-26 season, scoring 52 points (31G / 21A) in 58 games and will be relied upon heavily again for offence in 2026-27.

aleksander barkov.long: Barkov missed the entire 2025-26 season after undergoing surgery to repair ACL and MCL injuries. After a strenuous recovery, the 31-year-old Barkov was ready to return as an elite offensive producer, but he returned to the sidelines after suffering a lower-body injury in the second game of the season. Fortunately for Barkov, the injuries are unrelated, but he is still expected to miss about two months of hockey.

jonah gadjovich.det: Gadjovich will have surgery on his upper-body injury and will miss three months.

brad marchand.det: Marchand (lower-body) is expected to miss the next six weeks.
brad marchand.long: Just days after losing Aleksander Barkov (lower body), the Panthers' injury woes continued as Marchand exited Tuesday's game with a lower-body injury. Marchand began the season on the sidelines with an undisclosed injury and lasted only 9:36 on ice in his second game before suffering his latest ailment. Fortunately for Marchand and the Panthers, though he will miss some time, he is expected back in the lineup by late November.

brock faber.long: Minnesota's top-pair defensemen suffered a scary skull fracture in the Wilds' final preseason game and is expected to be out indefinitely after undergoing surgery on Tuesday. The 24-year-old's absence will be felt massively in Minnesota at the start of the season after he put up 15 goals, 51 points, and a +18 plus/minus in 80 games last season while averaging 24:41 TOI.

filip gustavsson.det: Gustavsson (hip) has been placed on LTIR.
filip gustavsson.long: Gustavsson underwent offseason hip surgery, and his recent placement on LTIR likely won't affect his eventual return to action. The 27-year-old Gustavsson is entering the first year of a five-year contract extension worth $38 million ($6.8 million AAV) and will be poised to outduel counterpart Jesper Wallstedt, Minnesota's de facto starting goalie.

nick foligno.det: Foligno has been placed on IR with an upper-body injury.
nick foligno.long: Foligno only played 3:29 time-on-ice in Tuesday's 3-2 loss to the Buffalo Sabres before exiting the game with an upper-body injury. The veteran 38-year-old forward has one goal through three games this season. Nico Sturm drew into Minnesota's lineup on Thursday as Foligno's replacement.

ivan demidov.det: Demidov (lower-body) will be out for the next two to four weeks.
ivan demidov.long: Demidov missed some time during training camp battling through a foot injury, but was able to suit up on time for Montreal's season opener. Now, the talented 20-year-old forward will return to the sidelines for two to four weeks, but it's unclear if the ailment is related to his previous one. Demidov has two points (1G / 1A) in two games this season.

sam montembeault.long: Montembeault did not finish practice on Wednesday due to a lower-body injury, and is expected to miss approximately two weeks. The 29-year-old goalie fell out of favour in Montreal last season and spent time in the AHL, but he has started the 2026-27 season in the NHL as Jakub Dobes' backup.

The 22-year-old defenseman, the Devils' 46th-overall pick in the 2022 NHL Entry Draft, spent most of the 2025-26 season in the AHL, where he tallied 19 points (1G / 18A) in 29 games with the Utica Comets.

mathew barzal.long: Barzal continues to work his way back from a knee injury that kept him out of training camp. He skated on his own on Thursday, which is a sign that he is getting closer to returning to practice with his teammates. The Islanders have yet to provide any kind of timeline on his return to the lineup.

alexander romanov.det: Romanov will undergo surgery to repair an ACL tear and miss 6-8 months.
alexander romanov.long: Romanov exited Tuesday's 5-2 loss to the New York Rangers after just 13:20 of ice time. He was absent from practice on Wednesday, and shortly after, the team announced that he would undergo surgery to repair an ACL tear in his right knee and miss six to eight months. The 26-year-old Romanov missed 67 games last season due to a shoulder injury and is likely to miss the remainder of this season as well, for an additional 81 games.

artem zub.det: Zub (knee) is expected to miss the start of the season.
artem zub.long: Senators' Head Coach Travis Green stated that Zub is still recovering from a knee injury from the postseason and is unlikely to be ready for the start of the 2026-27 campaign. The 30-year-old defenseman has battled injuries in his career, but his coming off of a career-best season, scoring 30 points (5G / 25A) in 81 games.

william eklund.det: The Senators are placing William Eklund (ankle) on IR.

kurtis macdermid.det: Kurtis MacDermid (upper-body) will begin the 2026-27 season as an injured/non-roster player.
kurtis macdermid.long: Ottawa will be without one of their toughest players to begin the 2026-27 season after they announced Kurtis MacDermid begin the year on the injured/non-roster player list due to an upper-body injury. The 32-year-old bruising forward last scored in the NHL in 2023-24 with Colorado, having appeared in over 58 games since he last found the back of the net.

jake sanderson.det: Sanderson (lower-body) skated on Thursday but will not play vs. Philadelphia.
jake sanderson.long: Sanderson skated on his own prior to Thursday's morning skate but will miss his third straight game with a lower-body injury that he suffered early in the season opener. Sanderson returning to the ice is a good sign that he's not expected to be sidelined long-term, but as of now the Senators have not provided a timetable for his return.

nikita grebenkin.det: Grebenkin (upper-body) has been placed on injured reserve.
nikita grebenkin.long: Grebenkin was a regular in Philadelphia's bottom-six last season, but his 2026-27 debut will have to wait a while longer after being placed on Injured Reserve. The 23-year-old forward recorded 14 points (4G / 10A) and 86 hits in 55 games last season. In a corresponding move, Denver Barkey has been activated from IR.

justin brazeau.det: Brazeau left Friday's practice with a lower-body injury.
justin brazeau.long: Brazeau's 2026-27 campaign is already off to a rough start after Pittsburgh announced on Friday that the 28-year-old bottom-six winger left practice with a lower-body injury and is uncertain of his status for the team's opener. Brazeau missed 18 games in 2025-26 due to injury but still put up an impressive 17 goals, 34 points and 104 SOG in 64 games in his first season in Pittsburgh.

ryan lindgren.det: Lindgren (upper-body) is expected to miss the next 4-6 weeks after being placed on IR on Thursday.
ryan lindgren.long: Lindgren exited Tuesday's game with an upper-body injury and has not been ruled out for the next four to six weeks. The 28-year-old Lindgren was a stabilizing presence on Seattle's blueline last season, averaging 18:20 time-on-ice, recording 118 blocks and scoring nine points (2G / 7A) in 76 games.

logan mailloux.det: Mailloux (right hand) underwent surgery and will be re-evaluated in eight weeks.
logan mailloux.long: Mailloux exited Saturday's preseason game after a fight with Chicago Blackhawks forward Cole Smith and did not return. He has since undergone surgery to address the injury and will likely miss at least eight weeks. It's an unfortunate blow for Mailloux, who began looking more comfortable toward the end of his rookie season in 2025-26 and was in line to take a step forward with the Blues in 2026-27.

tyler tucker.det: Tucker underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee and will be re-evaluated in six weeks.

alexey toropchenko.det: Toropchenko will be re-evaluated in six weeks for an upper-body injury.
alexey toropchenko.long: Toropchenko left Friday's season opener vs. Dallas with an upper-body injury and will now be forced to miss weeks after the team announced Sunday that the 27-year-old would be re-evaluated in six weeks for the injury. It is a tough loss for the sixth-year pro, who was looking for a bounce-back campaign after putting up four goals, 11 points and 68 SOG in 65 games last season.

yanni gourde.det: Gourde underwent hip surgery in the summer and is expected to be out until December.
yanni gourde.long: Gourde appeared in all 82 games last season, scoring nine goals and 19 assists (28 points) while playing a key role on the Lightning's checking line with Zemgus Girgensons and Pontus Holmberg. With Gourde expected to be out until December, he's expected to miss at least the first 26 games of the season.

nick blankenburg.det: Blankenburg will make his Maple Leafs’ debut vs. Colorado on Saturday.

elvis merzlikins.det: Merzlikins (shoulder) is expected to be out for another 3-to-5 months.
elvis merzlikins.long: Merzlikins was acquired from the Blue Jackets as a part of the Kirill Marchenko trade, and is reportedly not a part of the Maple Leafs' goaltending plans. They won't have to make a decision on him for roughly three months, as GM John Chayka said he'll need at least that much time as he continues to rehab from offseason shoulder surgery.

max domi.det: Domi (lower-body) has been added to LTIR.
max domi.long: Domi failed his preseason physical after offseason lower-body surgery and was placed on LTIR on Wednesday, saving the Maple Leafs $3.75 million in cap space. Domi appeared in 80 games for Toronto in 2025-26, picking up 12 goals, 36 points and 95 PIMs. He is without a timeline to return.

dakota joshua.det: Joshua is week-to-week with a core injury.
dakota joshua.long: Joshua has been battling a core injury for an extended period, limiting his presence at training camp. Last week, Maple Leafs GM John Chayka insisted Joshua was day-to-day, but has since changed his timeline to week-to-week. The 30-year-old Joshua had a decent inaugural season with the Maple Leafs in 2025-26, scoring 18 points (10G / 8A) and recording 195 hits while playing 55 games in a bottom-six role.

john tavares.long: Tavares was absent from practice on Friday, but it is unclear if he will be available when Toronto returns to action on Saturday against the Colorado Avalanche. The 36-year-old forward has three points (1G / 2A) through five games this season.

thatcher demko.det: Demko (hip) is hopeful to return before Christmas.
thatcher demko.long: Demko's 2025-26 season ended in January after a hip injury that required surgery, but he is hopeful to make his 2026-27 debut in December. Demko, who has battled a myriad of injuries in recent seasons, had a 2.90 GAA and .895 SV% in 20 appearances last season (8-10-1). The Canucks begin the 2026-27 season with Kevin Lankinen and Leevi Merilainen as their goaltending tandem.

victor olofsson.long: Olofsson played 10:48 of ice time in Tuesday's 6-2 win over the Seattle Kraken but exited the game with an undisclosed injury. The 31-year-old Swedish forward was off to a strong start to the 2026-27 season, scoring five points (4G / 1A) in four games, including a recent promotion to the Golden Knights' top power-play unit. Trevor Connelly took Olofsson's spot on the Golden Knights' top power-play unit at practice on Thursday.

rasmus sandin.det: Sandin underwent surgery to repair a torn ACL in his right knee and is expected to return in 6-9 months.
rasmus sandin.long: Sandin missed the final two games of the 2025-26 regular season, which will extend into the start of the 2026-27 season as he recovers from surgery to address an ACL tear. The 26-year-old Swedish defenseman has become an integral part of Washington's defence core, playing exclusively on one of the top two pairs. He averaged 19:12 time-on-ice and scored 29 points (5G / 24A) in 73 games this season.

matt roy.det: Roy (lower-body) is out vs. Pittsburgh and is considered day-to-day.
matt roy.long: Roy exited Saturday's game with a lower-body injury, and his status is day-to-day. The 31-year-old Roy averaged 20:37 time-on-ice, recording 19 points (2G /17A), 116 hits, and 146 blocks in 79 games last season. Dylan McIlrath will draw into the lineup as Roy's replacement on Wednesday.

elias salomonsson.det: Salomonsson remains in concussion protocol and is out vs. Seattle on Monday.
elias salomonsson.long: On Thursday, Salomonsson was on the receiving end of a heavy hit from Dallas Stars' forward Jason Robertson, and exited the game after only 8:56 time-on-ice due to concussion protocol. The 21-year-old first-year Swedish defenseman is averaging 17:58 time-on-ice and has five points (1G / 4A) in 32 games. He has not played since and will remain out of the lineup on Monday.

connor hellebuyck.det: Hellebuyck will start in Vegas on Monday.
connor hellebuyck.long: Hellebuyck struggled in his previous outing, allowing five goals on 20 shots (.750 SV%) in a 7-1 loss to the Philadelphia Flyers, severely crippling Winnipeg's slim playoff hopes. That said, they will need a win on Monday, along with some luck elsewhere in the league, to stay in the race. The 32-year-old Hellebuyck, the back-to-back reigning Vezina trophy winner, has had a largely disappointing 2025-26 season and hasn't been able to elevate his game at opportune times, including posting an ugly 2.81 GAA and .874 SV% in five games this month (3-2-0). The Jets enter Monday's contest as +150 road underdogs against the Vegas Golden Knights.

josh morrissey.det: Morrissey (upper-body) will be out on Friday vs. Anaheim and is considered day-to-day.
josh morrissey.long: Morrissey exited Wednesday's 3-2 win over the Colorado Avalanche after just 9:32 on ice with an upper-body injury. He will not play on Friday, but it is not expected to be a long-term issue. Expect Neal Pionk to take Morrissey's place on the Jets' top powerplay unit.
